official_sources.title: GDAL raster scale, offset and unit data model
official_sources.finding: GDAL raster bands may declare an offset, scale and unit so stored values can be converted into meaningful physical values such as elevation in metres.
official_sources.limitation: Scale, offset and unit metadata do not establish the vertical datum, and missing metadata cannot be guessed from value ranges.

official_sources.title: GDAL RasterBand raw-to-physical value formula
official_sources.finding: GDAL defines physical units value as raw value multiplied by scale plus offset and states that RasterIO and ReadBlock do not apply that conversion automatically.
official_sources.limitation: A caller must verify whether another library layer already applied decoding to avoid both omission and double application.

official_sources.title: GDAL exact versus approximate band minimum and maximum
official_sources.finding: GDAL ComputeRasterMinMax reads all pixels for an exact range when approximation is disabled; approximate mode may trust cached values or sample blocks, and nodata is excluded.
official_sources.limitation: Band-wide exact extrema are still not parcel extrema unless the exact geometry and mask support are applied first.

official_sources.title: GDAL minimum and maximum location tie behavior
official_sources.finding: GDAL minimum/maximum location computation ignores nodata and masked pixels, but when the same extreme occurs at several locations the returned location is unspecified.
official_sources.limitation: A single library-returned location cannot represent all tied extrema or support deterministic cross-version comparison.

official_sources.title: GDAL actual min-max and approximate statistics controls
official_sources.finding: GDAL raster info distinguishes actual min/max and all-pixel statistics from approximate statistics that may use overviews or a subset of pixels.
official_sources.limitation: Stored statistics can be stale or cover the complete band rather than the parcel window; exact native readback remains required.

official_sources.title: GDAL numeric data-type conversion rules
official_sources.finding: GDAL data-type conversion clips values assigned to narrower integer ranges, rounds floating values converted to integers, maps infinities to integer limits and maps NaN to zero.
official_sources.limitation: A successful RasterIO conversion can therefore conceal overflow, precision loss or invalid-data replacement unless the source and buffer data types are pinned.

official_sources.title: NumPy peak-to-peak signed-integer overflow warning
official_sources.finding: NumPy peak-to-peak preserves the input dtype, so signed-integer ranges larger than the positive capacity can wrap and be returned as negative values.
official_sources.limitation: Viewing an overflowed result as unsigned may reveal the bit pattern but does not replace explicit promotion before subtraction.

official_sources.title: NumPy NaN-aware extrema empty-support behavior
official_sources.finding: NumPy nanmax ignores NaN values but returns NaN and raises a RuntimeWarning for an all-NaN slice; nanmin has the corresponding behavior.
official_sources.limitation: Ignoring NaN alone does not apply GDAL mask, nodata sentinel, infinity or parcel geometry rules.
